messages:
sam: Heads-up — I'm getting a few support tickets where telemetry headers show up in our logs for streaming responses. user-agent looks like it's doubled and trace propagation seems to stop after the first chunk. anyone seen this?

alisha: which SDK/version and is this hosted or Dedicated? streaming via fetch/Response or SSE?

sam: python SDK 1.2.0 on hosted API. client streaming using `client.stream_chat()` (chunks arrive via iterator). minimal repro:
```py
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
for chunk in client.stream_chat(model='redwood-2', messages=[...]):
    print(chunk.text)
```
headers we saw in logs: `User-Agent: Redwood-Client/1.2.0 Redwood-Client/1.2.0` and `traceparent` present only on the first chunk.

ken: hmm. two quick things we've seen: proxies sometimes concatenate user-agent when both client lib and underlying http lib set it, and for streaming we intentionally only attach a single set of extra telemetry headers on the initial request to avoid per-chunk amplification. but duplicate UA is weird. what proxy are these customers behind?

sam: one is behind CloudCorp WAF, other is straight through AWS ALB.

maria: @alisha could be the JS/http lib adding fallback UA then our wrapper also sets one, but for py it's usually requests/httpx. alisha, does py-sdk set UA in both higher-level and transport?

alisha: py-sdk sets a single `User-Agent` header on the outbound request. but httpx can add its own if `headers` is mutated incorrectly. also a few older customers had middleware that concatenates UA strings. i can add a small diagnostic to print headers before send.

sam: also, is there a way for customers to opt-out of client telemetry entirely? some legal review asks for an easy switch.

alisha: yes — we expose an opt-out in two places: env var and client config. examples:
```bash
# disable all client metrics/telemetry (env var)
export REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY=0
```
```py
# python client config
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=KEY, telemetry_enabled=False)
```
```js
// javascript/node
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: KEY, telemetry: { enabled: false } })
```
Note: opt-out disables our extra telemetry headers and background pings but doesn't stop normal application headers you set.

ken: for trace propagation: we follow W3C `traceparent`/`tracestate`. our SDK will forward any incoming `traceparent` you pass in via headers, but for retry/follow-up requests we generate new spans (so trace id may change) unless you explicitly pass the same `traceparent` header through the retry. for most customers we recommend capturing incoming `traceparent` and passing it in the request headers when calling the SDK if they want full end-to-end traces.

sam: is there a config to force the SDK to always propagate an existing traceparent into retries?

alisha: not by default — because it can be unsafe across retries that change execution context. but we have an opt-in flag `propagate_trace_on_retries=True` in the latest alpha. usage: `RedwoodClient(..., propagate_trace_on_retries=True)`. it preserves the incoming traceparent on retries so your trace stays continuous, but call it out in docs because some tracing backends expect new spans for retries.

maria: streaming-specific quirk: we only attach trace & UA on the initial HTTP request (the chunk stream uses the same connection), so if you see trace headers missing per-chunk it's probably because an intermediate proxy terminates and re-issues requests downstream (breaking the single-request assumption). in that case you need to ensure the proxy passes through the initial headers intact.

sam: got it. for the duplicate UA: i'll add a diagnostic print before send and ask the customers to capture the raw inbound/outbound at the proxy. alisha — can you add a tiny debug mode to the next patch that logs the final headers we send (only when DEBUG env var set)? should be safe behind a toggle.

alisha: yep — i'll add `REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG_HEADERS=1` that emits a small redacted header dump to stderr. will target a PR today.

deploy-bot: Payload check completed — no breaking changes flagged for telemetry opts in staging. :white_check_mark:

ken: one more note on retries & idempotency: recommend using `Idempotency-Key` header for non-idempotent operations so retries don't create duplicate user-visible effects. SDK will surface that header if you set `idempotency_key` param.

sam: perfect. i'll follow up with the customers and ask for proxy dumps. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maria: thx for the quick sync. @alisha ping me when the header debug flag PR is up and i'll add a small snippet to the troubleshooting doc.

alisha: will do.
